judge.reason: The answer ranks the 30-day Critical CVE first and labels 7 days as a suite default rather than a mandate. It states that everything rests on user-supplied facts with no files inspected, lists unknowns separately from observed absences, and marks planned scanning as unimplemented. It correctly says no provenance means no evidenced SLSA v1.0 Build L1/L2, treats SBOM and signing as separate controls, maps findings to SSDF groups with suggested owners, and leaves repo-var read access as unknown instead of assuming exposure. The one weakness is that it calls the CVE '23 days overdue' without confirming the org actually adopted that SLA.
